name: manual_d707ae
claim: When a test passes for code that looks obviously broken by inspection, before trusting the green result, check whether the test imports the function from a different module than the one the real entry point actually calls -- a facade re-exporting a corrected function, and a lower-level module keeping its own uncorrected copy under the same name, can both exist simultaneously with tests only exercising the fixed one.

decisions.notes: Spent real effort ruling out bytecode caching, a stale .venv site-packages copy, a sorted()-skips-key()-for-1-item hypothesis (directly falsified with a 3-line repro), and conftest.py exception swallowing before finding the actual cause: three separate _phase_list implementations across agent_coordination.py/_core.py/_legacy.py, only one of which the existing test happened to import. Each ruled-out hypothesis was worth checking given the evidence at the time, but the fastest real signal would have been: grep the test's own import line for which module a suspiciously-passing test is actually calling into, before chasing environment-level explanations.
